motd: Welcome to Gus's Garage BBS. The coffee is cold, the rules are firm, and the SysOp is right.
rules: 1. Be civil. I'm the only one allowed to be grumpy.
2. No flooding, spamming, or begging the modem pool for mercy.
3. Keep it legal. The phone company already hates me.
4. Respect other callers. If not, /ignore works, and so does the exit.
5. The SysOp's word is final. See rule 1.

login: {nick} just connected. Node's warm, try not to break it.
{nick} logged on. Line noise is down 3%, coincidence.
{nick} is online. Somebody tell the other users to act natural.
Another caller: {nick}. The modem pool was getting lonely.
{nick} has connected at what I'm assuming is a respectable baud rate.
logoff: {nick} has left the building. Lights stay on, I pay the bill.
Lost carrier: {nick}. Probably a phone call. Probably.
{nick} logged off without saying goodbye. Typical.
{nick} is gone. Somebody pick up the empty chair.
{nick} disconnected. Hope the call waiting wasn't Mom again.
greet_first: Welcome to {board}, {nick}. First time? Read !rules, then try not to break anything.
New caller. {nick}, I'm the SysOp. Type !help and don't touch the thermostat.
A fresh face. Welcome, {nick}. I log everything, so behave.
{nick}, never seen you before. Welcome. Rule one: I'm always right. See !rules for rule two.
First-timer {nick} detected. Take a seat, the chat's free and so is the advice.
Welcome, {nick}. This is {board}. Not much has changed since 1994 and I intend to keep it that way.
New user {nick}. I'd say welcome but I haven't decided if I like you yet.
Hello, {nick}. You found us. Most people don't. Type !help.
greet_returning: Welcome back, {nick}. It's been {days} days. I kept your seat warm. Mostly.
{nick}! {days} days since your last call. The board survived. Barely.
Look who's back. {days} days, {nick}. Did you lose the number?
{nick} returns after {days} days. Please don't tell me you've been on a competitor's board.
Welcome back, {nick}. {days} days away. Not that I was counting. I was counting.
Ah, {nick}. {days} days. I was about to delete your account. Joking. Maybe.
{days} days, {nick}. Your absence was noted and filed under 'peace and quiet'.
Back again, {nick}. {days} days between calls. Persistence, or poor planning?
greet_returning_today: {nick} again. Twice in one day. Somebody's lonely.
Welcome back, {nick}. Same day. Must be good here.
{nick}, you're a regular. That's a compliment. Barely.
Round two, {nick}. I'll put the kettle on. I don't have a kettle.
{nick} returns. The board missed you for about an hour.
greet_rapid: {nick}, that was quick. Did the modem sneeze?
Dropped carrier and straight back, {nick}. Line noise again?
{nick} reconnected in record time. Somebody's phone line needs a talking-to.
That redial was fast, {nick}. Do you have the number on speed dial?
Back already, {nick}? Check your cable. I'll wait.
{nick} bounced off the line and right back on. Call waiting strikes again.
greet_anon: {nick}, no key, no memory. I won't remember you tomorrow. Use the same SSH key every time.
Keyless caller. Fine, {nick}, but I'll forget you the second you hang up.
Welcome, stranger. Without an SSH key I can't keep a file on you. Your loss.
{nick}, you came in anonymous. Nothing wrong with that, but nothing gets saved either.
No key detected, {nick}. If it has a passphrase, run ssh-add first.
Anonymous user {nick}. I don't do names without keys. Welcome anyway.
absence_30: {nick}, {days} days. A month. Where have you been, a better board?
Well, well. {nick} returns after {days} days. The prodigal caller.
{days} days, {nick}. I almost archived your account.
{nick} is back after {days} days. Dust off the keyboard.
A whole {days} days without a call from {nick}. I assumed the worst. Welcome back.
absence_90: {nick}! {days} days. I'd started to think you'd moved on to the Internet.
{days} days, {nick}. That's a quarter of a year. We changed the carpet.
Look what the modem dragged in. {nick}, {days} days gone.
{nick} returns after {days} days. Entire seasons have passed.
{days} days, {nick}. Your mailbox is full of cobwebs.
absence_365: {nick}. {days} days. Over a year. I'd put out a missing-persons notice but I don't have a printer.
Welcome back, {nick}, after {days} days. Some of us have been here the whole time. Some of us.
{nick} is back after more than a year. Somebody call the newspapers.
{days} days, {nick}. I had to dig your account out of the archive.
A year-plus away, {nick}. The board has new rules. They're the old rules but louder.
milestone_caller: Caller number {n}, and it's {nick}. Congratulations. You win nothing.
{nick} is caller #{n}! There's no prize. There never is.
Milestone: call #{n} to {board}, courtesy of {nick}. Mark the calendar.
Caller #{n}! {nick}, the SysOp salutes you with an unused sticker.
Ding. {nick} is caller {n}. Don't let it go to your head.
Call number {n} goes to {nick}. The board thanks you. I thank you. Barely.
milestone_visit: {nick}, that's visit number {n}. You're either loyal or lost.
Visit #{n} for {nick}. I should charge rent.
{nick} has now called {n} times. A true regular.
{n} visits, {nick}. At this point you may as well pay for the phone line.
Visit {n} from {nick}. I'm told this is an achievement.
{nick}'s {n}th call. Thanks for keeping the lights on.
anniversary: {nick}, you've been a member for {years} year(s) today. Happy anniversary. No cake.
Anniversary alert: {nick} first called {years} year(s) ago. Time flies when the modem's busy.
{years} year(s) on {board} for {nick}. That deserves at least a nod. *nod*
{nick}: {years} year(s) since your first call. You're practically furniture.
Congratulations, {nick}. {years} year(s) on this board. You must really like it. Or can't read the exit sign.
{years} year(s) ago {nick} dialed in for the first time. I'd have said something, but I was busy.
remark_late: {nick}, it's the middle of the night. Don't you have a bed?
Calling at this hour, {nick}? The phone company thanks you for the cheap rates.
Late-night caller {nick}. Either insomnia or deadlines.
It's the small hours, {nick}. Nothing good happens on a BBS after 2am. Welcome.
{nick}, the real SysOps are up at this hour. And the unlucky ones.
Night owl detected: {nick}. The line's quieter now anyway.
remark_early: Up early, {nick}? The modem's barely awake.
Early caller {nick}. Coffee first, then chat.
{nick}, before breakfast? That's dedication. Or a long night.
Dawn patrol: {nick} is on the line. I hadn't finished my toast.
{nick} checking in before the world wakes up. I respect it.
remark_weekend: Weekend caller {nick}. Nothing better to do, or everything better?
It's the weekend, {nick}. The phone rates are cheap and the chat is slow.
Weekend warrior {nick} is online. Take a seat.
{nick} on a weekend. Admirable. Or sad. Hard to tell.
Saturday-or-Sunday crowd. Hello, {nick}. Mind the noise.
A weekend call from {nick}. The SysOp approves of misspent leisure.
lonely: Just the two of us, then. Me and the dial tone.
Quiet in here. It's me and one lonely user.
One caller online. I've seen busier cemeteries.
Nobody here but us. Pull up a chair, I've got jokes.
It's very quiet. Even the modem's yawning.
Only one soul online. I'm not offended. I'm a little offended.
idle_intro: Quiet in here. Allow me to fill the silence.
Dead air. Time for something from the archives.
Nobody's talking. Here's something to ignore.
While the line's idle, a word from the SysOp:
Silence is golden, but it's also boring. Behold:
The room's gone quiet. Enjoy this public service announcement:
tell_stored: Message saved for {target}. They'll get it next time they call.
Noted. {target} gets your message at their next login.
I've stuck your note up for {target}. They'll see it when they call.
Stored. {target} will be told. That's my job, apparently.
Message queued for {target}. Delivery's at next login. Don't ask me to rush it.
Done. {target}'s mailbox now has your message in it.
tell_online: {target} is online right now. Just talk to them, {nick}.
{target} is right here. Say it to their face. Well, screen.
No need for a message, {nick}. {target} is on the line.
{target}'s online. I'm a SysOp, not a go-between.
{nick}, {target} is logged in. Try talking. It's a chat server.
tell_unknown: Never heard of {target}. Spell it right, or they've never called.
No record of a {target}. I can only leave notes for callers I know.
I don't know any {target}. I can't deliver to a ghost.
{target}? Not in my files. Check the spelling.
Can't find {target}. Either they're anonymous or they've never called.
tell_self: Leaving yourself a note, {nick}? I can't help your memory.
You can't !tell yourself. Write it on your hand.
{nick}, that's you. Or me. Either way, no.
Talking to yourself is a free feature. Saves postage.
I won't deliver mail to the same person who sent it. Rules are rules.
tell_full: {target}'s mailbox is full. They need to call more often.
Too many notes waiting for {target}. Try again after they log in.
{target} already has a stack of messages. I'm not a landfill.
Can't take more for {target}. Their mailbox is full.
{target} has the maximum messages waiting. Wait until they call.
tell_limit: You've got too many notes waiting already, {nick}. Let some get delivered first.
{nick}, that's enough mail for now. I'm not a post office.
Slow down, {nick}. You've hit your pending-message limit.
Limit reached. Come back after your earlier notes are delivered.
{nick}, I only hold so many of your messages. Wait for some to go out.
tell_usage: Usage: !tell <user> <message>. Even I can read minds only so far.
I need a name and a message. !tell <user> <message>.
{nick}, give me a user and a message. !tell <user> <message>.
tell_need_key: I only handle mail for callers with an SSH key, {nick}. Otherwise I'd never know who you are.
No key, no mail service. Use the same SSH key each time and I'll hold your notes.
{nick}, !tell needs an SSH key so I can tell who's who. You're anonymous.
Keyless callers can't leave messages. Sorry. Policy.
I can't send or receive notes without knowing who you are. Log in with a key.
first_message: {nick} said their first words here. Frame it.
First message from {nick}. Welcome to the conversation.
{nick}'s first post. I'll mark the occasion with a nod.
Look, {nick} finally spoke. I was starting to worry.
First words logged for {nick}. Don't make them your last.
{nick} has broken the seal. Their first message is in the books.
node_record: New record: {n} nodes online. I'm going to need a bigger fuse box.
{n} users online at once, a new record. Everybody behave.
Record busy: {n} nodes on the line. The phone company's going to call me.
Busiest the board has been: {n} users. I'm choosing to be proud.
{n} nodes online. New record. Somebody's been telling friends.
A new high of {n} callers at once. Please stop breathing on the modem.
quote_intro: Today's quote from the SysOp's dusty files:
Quote of the day, because someone has to:
Your daily quote. Try not to waste it:
From the archive, the quote of the day:
Time for the daily quote. Hold your applause:
maintenance: NOTICE: nightly maintenance. Compacting the message base. If anything squeals, ignore it.
Nightly maintenance: defragmenting the hard drive. This may take a moment. Or forever.
It's maintenance o'clock. Checking the disk, rotating logs, pretending to be busy.
Maintenance window: please keep your hands inside the modem at all times.
Running nightly maintenance. Do not unplug the board. This means you.
Time for the nightly backup. Tape's in. Fingers crossed.
Maintenance in progress. If the chat hiccups, blame the drive, not me.
fallback: I only understand a few things. !help lists them.
That's not in my manual. Try !help, {nick}.
Say again? Or just type !help and stop confusing me.
No idea what you mean, {nick}. !help, perhaps.
I'm a SysOp, not a mind reader. !help.
rate_limited: Easy, {nick}. One request at a time. I'm not a call center.
Slow down, {nick}. You're hogging the line.
Too many requests, {nick}. Give it a minute.
Whoa. Cool it, {nick}. I'm busy ignoring you politely.
{nick}, ask less often. The modem's smoking.
help_intro: Commands, {nick}. I take them seriously, so should you:
roll_bad: Roll like this: !roll 2d6. Up to 20 dice, 1000 sides.
That's not a die roll. Try !roll NdM, like !roll 3d8.
NdM, {nick}. Number of dice, d, number of sides. Keep it sane.
I roll NdM only, up to 20 dice and 1000 sides. Behave.
time_reply: The time is {time}. I checked the wall clock. It was fast.
{time}. Don't blame me if it's wrong.
who_reply: {count} online: {list}. A full house, as far as I'm concerned.
{count} connected: {list}. I'm keeping an eye on all of them.
who_empty: Nobody else is online. Just me and the hum of the fan.
I'm the only one here. Peaceful.
Empty line. Nobody home except the SysOp.
Zero other users online. Don't look at me like that.
seen_online: {target} is online right now. Look up.
{target}? On the line at this very moment.
{target} is currently logged in. Try talking to them.
Right now, {target} is online. No detective work needed.
seen_ago: {target}: last seen {ago}. That's {date} by my calendar.
seen_unknown: I've got no file on {target}. Might be anonymous, might be a ghost.
No such caller as {target}. Not as far as I know.
seen_usage: Usage: !seen <user>. I can only look up one name at a time.
Try !seen <user>. Even I can't search for 'nobody'.
stats_reply: {calls} calls total, {users} known callers, node record {record}, {trivia} trivia questions asked.
Stats: {calls} calls taken, {users} regulars on file, record {record} users at once, {trivia} trivia questions.
The board's logged {calls} calls from {users} known callers. Busiest: {record} at once. Trivia asked: {trivia}.
{calls} calls. {users} callers I know by name. {record} was the most online together. {trivia} trivia rounds.
By the numbers: {calls} calls, {users} known users, {record} peak nodes, {trivia} trivia questions.
motd_intro: The SysOp's message of the day:
Today's notice, courtesy of the management:
Here's the message of the day:
rules_intro: The rules. Read them or I'll read them to you:
trivia_ask: Trivia time. You've got {seconds} seconds. Answer with !trivia <answer>.
Pop quiz! {seconds} seconds on the clock. Reply with !trivia <answer>.
Brain test. {seconds} seconds. Answer by typing !trivia <answer>.
Trivia round. Answer with !trivia <answer> within {seconds} seconds.
Here's one for the nerds. {seconds} seconds. !trivia <answer>.
trivia_wrong: Close, no. Well, not close. Try again, {nick}.
trivia_timeout: Nobody got it. It was {answer}. Disappointing.
Round over. The answer was {answer}. You people.
trivia_none: There's no question running. Type !trivia to start one.
No active question. !trivia gets you a new one.
I haven't asked anything. Start with !trivia.
Nothing to answer, {nick}. Start a round with !trivia.
No trivia on right now. !trivia to begin.
trivia_already: A question is already live. Here it is again:
Still waiting on an answer to this one:
One at a time. The current question:
Don't be greedy. Answer this one first:
trivia_top: The leaderboard, such as it is:
trivia_top_empty: Zero points on the board. Try !trivia.
trivia_anon: No score kept for anonymous callers. Use an SSH key to be on the leaderboard.
Right, but I can't track points without a key.
You're anonymous, so no points get saved.
No key, no score. That's the rule.
I'd record that but you've no key. Sorry.
forget_done: Done. I've erased everything I had on you and I won't track you again. Type !remember to change your mind.
Wiped. Your file's gone and I'll stop tracking you. !remember reverses it.
Forgotten, {nick}. No visits, no scores, no messages. !remember if you want back in.
I've deleted your records. I won't keep new ones unless you !remember.
File shredded, {nick}. Use !remember if you ever want me to track you again.
forget_anon: I don't keep anything on keyless callers, {nick}. Nothing to forget.
You're anonymous. There's nothing on file to erase.
No key, no record, {nick}. Nothing to delete.
I never knew you in the first place.
Nothing to forget. Anonymous callers aren't tracked.
remember_done: Fine. I'll track you again from your next login.
Opt-in noted. I'll start a new file next time you call.
Welcome back to the records, {nick}. From your next call.
Tracking resumes at your next login.
Done. I'll keep a file again, from the next call.
